title: Return Premium Basis and Reinstatement Fee by HomeGuard Package
content:
Tariff sheet, HomeGuard Homeowners Policy. When the named insured cancels midterm, each package returns unearned premium on its own basis, may keep a short-rate share, and keeps a minimum earned premium; each package also sets the fee charged when a cancelled policy is reinstated.

## Tariff

| Package | Return basis on a named-insured midterm cancellation | Short-rate retention (percent of the pro-rata unearned premium) | Minimum earned premium (USD) | Reinstatement fee (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HomeGuard HO-3 Essential | short rate | 10 | 100.00 | 25.00 |
| HomeGuard HO-3 Enhanced | pro rata | 0 | 75.00 | 25.00 |
| HomeGuard HO-3 Premier | pro rata | 0 | 50.00 | 25.00 |
| HomeGuard HO-5 Enhanced | pro rata | 0 | 75.00 | 25.00 |
| HomeGuard HO-5 Premier | pro rata | 0 | 50.00 | 0.00 (none) |
| HomeGuard HO-5 Signature | pro rata | 0 | 0.00 | 0.00 (none) |

## Terms

1. The return basis states how unearned premium is returned when the named insured cancels midterm: pro rata or short rate.
2. The short-rate retention is the share of the pro-rata unearned premium the company retains on a short-rate cancellation. It is 0 on every package whose basis is pro rata; HomeGuard HO-3 Essential is the only short-rate package, at 10 percent.
3. The minimum earned premium is the premium the company keeps at minimum on a named-insured midterm cancellation.
4. The reinstatement fee is charged when a cancelled policy is reinstated; 0.00 means no fee.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

A hypothetical HomeGuard HO-3 Essential policy has a pro-rata unearned premium of 600.00 at cancellation by the named insured. The company retains 10 percent of it, 60.00, and the remaining 540.00 is the returnable amount on the short-rate basis. The same 600.00 on a hypothetical HomeGuard HO-3 Enhanced policy is returnable in full on the pro-rata basis, the retention there being 0.
